title: Stork Avocado Drop Challenge
description: A stork flies across the sky carrying avocados that the player must drop into floating baskets below. The player controls the stork's horizontal position with arrow keys, adjusts altitude with W/S keys, and presses spacebar to release avocados at the right moment to land them in moving target zones. Score points by landing avocados in baskets across increasingly difficult rounds.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Stork Avocado Drop game. Load stork.glb as the player-controlled bird and Avocado.glb as the droppable projectile. Setup: Use a perspective camera angled slightly downward. Add a gradient sky background using a large sphere with shader material. Create a ground plane with green color. Place 3 circular target baskets (flat cylinders with ring geometry borders) on the ground that slowly move left and right at varying speeds. Add directional light plus ambient light for good visibility. Display an HTML overlay showing score, current round (1-5), and remaining avocados (starts at 5 per round). Game mechanics: The stork flies at an adjustable altitude. Use left/right arrow keys to move the stork horizontally with clamped boundaries. Use W/S keys to raise or lower the stork altitude between a min and max height. Press spacebar to release an avocado from the stork's position. The avocado must fall with simulated gravity (acceleration of 9.8 units/s²), rotating as it drops. Detect collision between falling avocados and basket targets using distance checks. A successful landing adds 10 points multiplied by the current round number. A miss subtracts no points but wastes an avocado. After each avocado lands or misses, spawn a new one attached to the stork if supply remains. Validation: Clamp stork position within scene bounds. Validate altitude stays within range. Prevent spacebar spam by requiring 1-second cooldown between drops. Track round progression: after 5 drops, advance to next round where baskets move faster and shrink slightly. After round 5, display a final score screen with a restart button. Add subtle wing-flap animation to the stork by oscillating its rotation. Scale the avocado model to roughly 1/4 the stork size.
